h1: The 7 Best Small Safes for Offices, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Safes for Offices: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 small safes for offices, scored on laptop-size interiors, shared access codes, desk-drawer fit and mounting hardware.
summary: The SentrySafe Shelf Safe is the office pick for anyone who needs to lock up a laptop: its interior is the widest here and its keypad has a light. The Bonsaii 0.6 cu ft safe is the better all-rounder for documents and cash, and the Amazon Basics 0.5 cu ft gives you a mountable shelf layout. For a desk drawer, the Amazon Basics Slim fits inside it. The Digital Electronic Money Safe suits two staff with separate codes.
intro: An office safe has a problem a home safe does not: more than one person needs it, and nobody remembers who knows the code. A shared four-digit number that the last three employees all learned becomes a formality, not security. The right small safe for an office is the one that lets two people use it without one revealing a code to the other.

We ranked seven small safes against that problem and the usual office contents: cash boxes, petty cash, a laptop, passports and key documents. Interior size, code options, mounting and backup entry led the scoring. None of the listings claim fire protection, and the SentrySafe says outright that it is not fireproof, so these are theft deterrents and not fire safes.

products.name: SentrySafe Shelf Safe with Digital Keypad Lock, Steel Safe with Interior Light
products.verdict: The widest interior here, laptop-rated, with a light and bolt-down hardware.
products.description:
The SentrySafe has a 16.8 by 11.6 by 6.9 inch interior, the widest in this ranking and rated to hold a laptop. It has a digital keypad, an interior light and bolt-down hardware, and the listing says it is not fireproof.

Offices lose laptops more often than cash, and this is the only safe here sized for one. The interior light helps when the safe sits low under a desk. Bolting it down matters more in an office than at home, where a visitor could simply lift a loose box. It ranks first despite the $100 to $200 price because nothing else here fits a laptop.

Buy it if you secure a laptop with documents and cash. The caveat: it is not fireproof, so keep irreplaceable papers elsewhere.
products.idealFor: Offices that need to lock a laptop alongside documents and cash.
products.skipIf: You only keep small cash and want to spend less.

products.name: Bonsaii Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Home Office, 0.6 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: A 0.6 cu ft box with two 18mm steel bolts and three ways to open it.
products.description:
Bonsaii's 0.6 cu ft safe has a removable shelf, two 18mm steel locking bolts and three ways in: code, key or USB-C emergency power.

The two steel bolts are the security detail that sets it apart in a group that mostly says steel box. It is also the roomiest of the small safes below the SentrySafe. The three entry methods help an office: the manager can hold the key while staff use the code, and USB-C power gets the door open after a battery failure. It ranks second because it lists no laptop-sized interior.

Buy it if you store documents, a cash box and small devices. The caveat is that a 0.6 cu ft interior will not take a laptop.
products.idealFor: Offices storing documents, cash and small devices.
products.skipIf: You need to lock up a laptop.

products.name: Amazon Basics Steel Security Safe and Lock Box with Electronic Keypad
products.verdict: A 0.5 cu ft safe with four expansion bolts and an adjustable shelf.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics safe holds 0.5 cu ft, with an adjustable removable shelf, three operation indicator lights, a carpeted floor and four expansion bolts for mounting.

Fixing a safe to the structure is the first office security step, and this is the one that comes with the hardware to do it. The adjustable shelf lets you split a drawer-sized space between cash and files, and the indicator lights show lock status and battery state. It ranks third because it lacks the Bonsaii's listed key and USB-C backup, and the interior is smaller.

Buy it if you plan to bolt a safe to a wall or floor. The caveat: there is no stated backup entry, so check what happens when batteries die.
products.idealFor: Offices that will bolt the safe to a wall or floor.
products.skipIf: You need a laptop-size interior or a key override.

products.name: Amazon Basics Small Slim Desk Drawer Security Safe with Programmable Electronic
products.verdict: A slim safe made to sit inside an existing desk drawer.
products.description:
This slim Amazon Basics safe fits inside a desk drawer, with a programmable electronic keypad, an emergency key and a mounting option inside the drawer itself.

The drawer fit is why an office would choose it: it disappears into furniture you already own, and a thief opening the drawer sees a plain box. The emergency key is a backup that the larger Amazon Basics lacks. It ranks fourth because slim means small, and a drawer-mounted safe is only as secure as the drawer that holds it.

Buy it if you want discreet storage for a cash box, passport and small items. The caveat is capacity, and a thin drawer will not stop a determined thief.
products.idealFor: Desk workers who want discreet storage in an existing drawer.
products.skipIf: You need to store documents or a laptop.

products.name: Digital Electronic Money Safe, Steel Security Lock Box with Keypad, Office
products.verdict: A 4.6L steel box that supports two independent codes for two staff members.
products.description:
This 4.6L SPCC steel box is mountable, supports 2 independent access codes and includes an anti-scratch carpet liner and a manual.

Two independent codes are the feature to look at. Each of two staff members keeps their own code, so you can change one without disturbing the other, solving the shared-code problem in the intro. It ranks fifth because 4.6L is small, enough for a cash box and a few items, and the security detail is thin.

Buy it if two people share a petty-cash box. The caveat: a 4.6L steel box is a deterrent, not a vault.
products.idealFor: Two employees sharing a petty-cash box.

products.name: MAESTON Mini Electronic Safe Box with Digital Keypad & Keys, 0.23 Cubic
products.verdict: A 0.23 cu ft safe with a 3 to 8 digit code and a magnetic auto-lock door.
products.description:
The MAESTON mini safe holds 0.23 cu ft, accepts a customizable 3 to 8 digit password, is mountable with a magnetic auto-lock door, and includes keys, 4 pre-drilled holes and 2 expansion bolts.

The code length is the security gain: an 8 digit code has far more combinations than a typical 4 digit one, which matters where several people walk past. The magnetic door closes itself, so it can't be left unlocked by accident. It ranks sixth because the interior is small and the listing gives little about steel gauge.

Buy it if you want longer codes and an auto-locking door on a compact box. The caveat: the 0.23 cu ft space holds only small items.
products.idealFor: Small offices that want a longer code on a compact box.
products.skipIf: You store documents or need two user codes.

products.name: Yuanshikj Small Steel Security Safe Box with Keypad, Key, 0.23 CuFt, Black
products.verdict: The lowest-cost mountable safe, with two emergency keys.
products.description:
The Yuanshikj is a 0.2 cu ft steel box with a keypad, a magnetic auto-lock door, a corrosion-resistant powder coat and two emergency keys, priced under $25.

Two emergency keys let a manager and an assistant each hold a backup, which is more than most budget safes offer. The powder coat resists the dings of a busy office, and the lowest price in the group makes it an easy first safe. It ranks last because the 0.2 cu ft interior is the smallest and it has no extras like lights or longer codes.

Buy it if you need a simple lockable box for a single desk. The caveat: it is a basic deterrent, so mount it.
products.idealFor: Single-desk use that needs a cheap, lockable box.
products.skipIf: You need more space or shared-code options.

methodology.title: Interior size
methodology.description: A laptop-size interior ranked first, then 0.6 and 0.5 cu ft documents boxes, then compact cash safes.

methodology.title: Shared access
methodology.description: Independent codes, longer codes and key backup were credited because offices have more than one user.

methodology.title: Mounting hardware
methodology.description: Expansion bolts, bolt-down kits and pre-drilled holes decided how well each can resist being carried away.

methodology.title: Backup entry
methodology.description: Key override or USB-C emergency power counted, since a locked-out office loses working time.

methodology.title: Honest limits
methodology.description: Missing fire ratings and thin lock detail were marked down, not assumed.

whatMatters.detail: What fits inside depends on the interior, not the outside size, because thick steel walls and door bolts eat space. A laptop needs about 16 by 11 inches, and only the SentrySafe offers that. Measure the items you plan to lock up and compare them with the interior dimensions in the listing, not cubic feet alone.

In an office, a code known to many people stops being a secret, and you cannot tell who opened the box. Safes with two independent codes, such as the Digital Electronic Money Safe, give each person their own. Look for independent codes or longer passwords, like the MAESTON's 3 to 8 digits, and change them whenever someone leaves.

A safe that is not fixed down can be carried out in a bag, which makes its lock irrelevant. Expansion bolts and pre-drilled holes anchor it to a desk, wall or floor, as with the Amazon Basics 0.5's four bolts. Check what hardware is included, and fix it into solid material, not thin partition board.

Keypad safes run on batteries, and a flat battery on a Monday morning means a locked box with your documents inside. A key, as on the Bonsaii and Yuanshikj, or the Bonsaii's USB-C power, gets you in. Look for backup access in the listing and keep the spare key somewhere other than the safe.

A fire rating is a tested standard that small keypad safes rarely carry, and thin steel alone does not stop heat from cooking paper or drives. The SentrySafe listing says it is not fireproof. If paper records matter, look for a named rating on the listing, and otherwise store backups off-site.

faq.q: Will these safes protect a laptop?
faq.a: Only the SentrySafe has a laptop-rated interior at 16.8 by 11.6 inches. The Bonsaii 0.6 and Amazon Basics 0.5 hold documents, cash and small devices but will not take a standard laptop, so measure yours before choosing.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with an office safe?
faq.a: Sharing one code among many people. The Digital Electronic Money Safe supports two independent codes, and the MAESTON allows 3 to 8 digits. Use longer codes, give each staff member a separate one where possible, and change them when staff leave.

faq.q: Is the Bonsaii 0.6 worth it over the Amazon Basics 0.5?
faq.a: If backup access matters, yes. The Bonsaii adds a key and USB-C emergency power plus two 18mm steel bolts, while the Amazon Basics provides four expansion bolts, an adjustable shelf and three indicator lights. Pick on how you would open it with a dead battery.

faq.q: How do I install a desk drawer safe?
faq.a: Remove the drawer contents, position the Amazon Basics Slim at the back, and fix it with the supplied hardware through the drawer base so it cannot be lifted out. Program the code and confirm the emergency key opens it before you load valuables.

faq.q: How often should I change the code?
faq.a: Whenever someone with access leaves, and at least once a year. Replace batteries at the same time, so the Bonsaii or SentrySafe keypad does not die during a busy week and force you to use the backup key or USB-C route.

faq.q: Can these safes survive a fire?
faq.a: Do not count on it. No listing claims fire protection, and the SentrySafe explicitly says it is not fireproof. Keep fire-critical documents such as deeds or backup drives in a rated fire safe or a bank box instead.

finalTake: The SentrySafe Shelf Safe is the best small safe for offices because it is the only one sized for a laptop, with an interior light and bolt-down hardware. The Bonsaii 0.6 cu ft is the better choice for documents and cash, and the Digital Electronic Money Safe suits two users. Mount whichever you buy, and remember that none is listed as fireproof.
